Pivot\\n\\n1. **Stagnation Signals Are Structural, Not Semantic (primary contribution)**: 系统性对比发现 agent stagnation 信号本质是结构性的——30 个结构特征（命令重复率、唯一命令比、文件 diff 频率等）在 in-domain (RF 0.9951) 和 cross-agent (GB 0.967) 都近完美预测停滞，全面优于 NL embedding probe (in-domain 0.906, cross-domain 0.751) 和 LLM-as-judge (+24.3pp)。Encoder-agnostic（3 个 encoder 均 >0.90）；最优窗口 k=5 (0.9309)；data scaling 10%→100% 单调递增。这揭示：(a) stagnation detection 不需要语义理解——简单结构特征已足够；(b) 结构特征天然跨 agent 迁移（不依赖 embedding domain adaptation）；(c) NL embedding 对 stagnation detection 无增量价值。**改变社区对 agent monitoring 方法选型的认知：从昂贵的表示学习转向轻量结构监控。** Gold set 验证 structural features 是否检测到真实 stagnation（非仅 circular eval artifact）是论文成立的关键。\\n\\n2. **LF Temporal Dynamics Are Systematic but Agent-Specific (analytical contribution)**: LFs 在 trajectory 上展现**系统性但 agent-specific 的**时序角色。SWE-Agent 上：cmd_rep leading (-1.87步)、file_diff concurrent (-1.2步)、OB lagging (+6.7步)。**OH 上 cmd_rep 角色反转**（从 leading 变 lagging +3.32步），而 file_diff（leading, -4.9步）和 OB（lagging, +18.1步）跨域一致。**消融验证：去掉 cmd_rep 后 OH F1 从 0.7512 飙升到 0.9272（+17.6pp）**，证明 cmd_rep 在 OH 上是噪声源而非信号。根因：cmd_rep 在 OH 上 92.3% firing rate + 71% FP，失去区分性。这揭示 LF 行为与 agent 架构之间的交互效应——为 weak supervision pipeline 在 sequential agent data 上的设计提供实证指导。同时量化 circular evaluation 问题：structural features 以 0.9951 F1 逆向工程 LF 标签，证明 LF-derived labels 上的高分不等于真实检测能力。\\n\\n3. **Temporal Label Model: A Well-Motivated Negative Finding (D039 negative result)**: 标准 data programming（majority vote）在 agent trajectory 上违反 i.i.d. 假设——LFs 产生系统性时序动态，这 motivate 了 temporal label model（TLM）的开发。然而，三种 TLM 实现**均未能超越简单 MV**：(a) **TWV（时序加权投票）**：绝大多数 σ 下有害（twv-ablation）；唯一微弱正向的 σ=2 训练的下游分类器全面劣化（in-domain -4.9pp, cross-agent -21.7pp, conf≥2 -1.8pp）(structural-on-twv)；(b) **HMM-TLM**：stagnation class overpredict；(c) **Lag-aware HMM**：仅追平 MV（0.8936）。**结论**：在当前 3-LF、低冲突（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）的 regime 下，temporal alignment 的收益被噪声引入抵消。TWV 改变的主要是低置信标签，但改变方向是错的。这是对 \\\"i.i.d. violation → temporal model must help\\\" 这一直觉的重要否定，为未来 temporal label model 研究提供了关键约束条件。\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: LLM agents 在长期任务中频繁\\\"语义停滞\\\"——执行看似合理但集体无效的动作序列。每个动作可能非重复、局部合理，但整个窗口缺乏 goal-directed progress。现有方法要么检测结构性循环（漏掉语义多样的停滞），要么做 step-level scoring（丢失窗口内的时序动态），要么依赖 LLM 自我评估（高开销 + 受困模型的判断力受限）。\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: (a) Cycle detectors（CDCS+CDSA, SpecRA, TrajAD）捕获重复/异常但漏掉语义多样的停滞；(b) Process Reward Models — **AgentPRM (Xi et al., ACM Web 2026, arxiv 2511.08325)** 是最直接的竞争者：用 TD/GAE 训练 step-level PRM 评估 \\\"promise and progress\\\"，但需要 outcome labels + RL pipeline，是 training signal 而非 monitoring tool。另有 PRM framework (arxiv 2502.10325)、ToolPRMBench (arxiv 2601.12294)、trajectory-level reward modeling (arxiv 2604.08178)。PRM 方向在 2025-2026 非常拥挤，我们的差异：**不需要 outcome labels**、**window-level 捕获 temporal dynamics**、**monitoring 而非 training**；(c) Self-reflection（Reflexion, LATS, Tree of Thoughts）依赖被困模型的自我评估，且是 intervention 而非 monitoring；(d) RL value functions (CodeRL) 需要 reward shaping；(e) **Agent monitoring 新方向**：\\\"Monitoring LLM Agents for Sequentially Contextual Harm\\\" (ICLR 2025 Workshop) 论证了 sequence-level monitoring 的必要性（单步分析不够）；\\\"Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring\\\" (arxiv 2508.19461) 研究了弱模型监控强 agent，但关注 safety 而非 progress；(f) **Agent degradation benchmark**：SlopCodeBench (arxiv 2603.24755, 2026) 量化了 coding agent 在长期任务中的退化——verbosity 90% 轨迹上升、erosion 80%——为我们的 problem motivation 提供了最新实证。\\n\\n- **Our framing (D039 Pivot)**: Progress stagnation detection 的系统性实证研究。**三层贡献**：(1) **Structural Signal Discovery Analysis** — 量化 LFs 在 agent trajectory 上的时序角色 + 跨 agent 迁移分析 + circular evaluation 问题的方法论贡献——为 sequential data 上的 weak supervision 提供实证指导；(3) **TLM Negative Finding** — 系统性测试三种 temporal label model 实现，均未超越 MV，提供重要的负面结果和 failure analysis——约束未来研究方向。\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"We present a systematic empirical study of progress stagnation detection in LLM agents through weak supervision. Our central finding is that stagnation signals are fundamentally structural: simple features (command repetition ratio, file diff frequency) achieve 0.995 in-domain and 0.967 cross-agent F1, decisively surpassing both neural embedding approaches (0.906/0.751) and LLM-as-judge baselines. Our results redirect agent monitoring from expensive representation learning and complex label models toward lightweight structural approaches.\\\"\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n- **EMNLP vs ICSE**: 核心 LFs 和数据 100% 来自 SE 领域。贴合 NLP venue 的策略：(a) weak supervision on sequential data 是通用方法论，适用于任何有时序结构的标注场景——data programming / Snorkel 出自 NLP 社区；(b) structural vs semantic signal 的发现对任何 agent monitoring 系统有指导意义；(c) circular evaluation 问题是 weak supervision 评估的通用挑战；(d) TLM negative finding 对 sequential label model 研究有方法论价值。\\n- **Reviewer lottery**: 遇到 SE-skeptical 的 NLP reviewer 可能被判 \\\"more suitable for ICSE/FSE\\\"——通过强化方法论洞见的跨域普适性和 LLM agent 社区的 NLP 属性来降低风险。\\n- **\\\"Negative finding paper 不够 novel\\\"**: 论文不是纯 negative finding——structural signal discovery (Claim 1) 是强正面结果；TLM negative finding pipeline（昂贵），我们是 monitoring tool + weak supervision pipeline（轻量）；PRM 是 step-level training signal，我们是 window-level detection。\\n- **\\\"Why not LLM-as-judge?\\\"**: 已有 baseline 对比——structural approach 维度：real-time inference、end-to-end deployment、gold set 上的对比。Gold set 是最终裁判 |\\n| TLM negative finding 不够有 contribution | Failure analysis 详细到足以约束未来研究：(1) 3-LF 低冲突 regime（conf≥2 一致率 95.1%）限制了 temporal alignment 的改进空间；(2) TWV 在低置信区改变标签方向错误；(3) 三种不同实现排除了实现偏差。论文同时有强正面结果（Claim 1, 2） |\\n| 跨 agent 迁移只测了两个 SE agent | Two-agent scope 在 Limitations 讨论 + structural features 跨域 0.967 的强迁移证据。Future work 包含 #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Zero-shot cross-agent evaluation: apply SWE-agent trained probe to OpenHands data.

Loads the GRU probe checkpoint trained on SWE-agent trajectories and evaluates
on OpenHands trajectory embeddings without any fine-tuning.

Also runs all baselines (Random, Majority, CosineSim, Repeat-3) and LF Oracle variants.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
from baselines import ALL_BASELINES, compute_metrics
from probe_model import ProgressProbe, WindowDataset, collate_fn
from labeling_functions import ALL_LFS, ABSTAIN


LF_NAMES = [name for name, _ in ALL_LFS]


def load_windows_with_labels(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    windows = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                windows.append(json.loads(line))
    return windows


def build_traj_step_index(traj_path: str) -> dict:
    """row_index -> list of step dicts."""
    index = {}
    with open(traj_path) as f:
        for i, line in enumerate(f):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            raw = json.loads(line)
            steps = []
            for s in raw.get("trajectory") or []:
                steps.append({"role": s.get("role", "unknown"), "text": s.get("text") or ""})
            index[i] = steps
    return index


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate_probe(model, loader, device):
    model.eval()
    all_labels, all_preds, all_probs = [], [], []
    for padded, labels, lengths in loader:
        logits = model(padded.to(device), lengths)
        probs = torch.sigmoid(logits)
        preds = (probs >= 0.5).long().cpu()
        all_labels.extend(labels.long().tolist())
        all_preds.extend(preds.tolist())
        all_probs.extend(probs.cpu().tolist())
    return compute_metrics(all_labels, all_preds), all_preds, all_probs


def compute_lf_predictions(windows, prior):
    """Compute LF Oracle variants."""
    fallback = 1 if prior >= 0.5 else 0

    def majority_vote(w):
        ml = w.get("majority_label", -1)
        return ml if ml != -1 else fallback

    def any_stag(w):
        vals = [w["labels"][lf] for lf in LF_NAMES]
        if 0 in vals:
            return 0
        if any(v != -1 for v in vals):
            return 1
        return fallback

    def all_agree(w):
        active = [w["labels"][lf] for lf in LF_NAMES if w["labels"][lf] != -1]
        if active and len(set(active)) == 1:
            return active[0]
        return fallback

    def single_lf(w, lf_name):
        v = w["labels"][lf_name]
        return v if v != -1 else fallback

    strategies = {
        "LF Majority Vote": [majority_vote(w) for w in windows],
        "LF Any-Stagnation": [any_stag(w) for w in windows],
        "LF All-Agreement": [all_agree(w) for w in windows],
    }
    for lf_name in LF_NAMES:
        strategies[f"Single LF: {lf_name}"] = [single_lf(w, lf_name) for w in windows]

content.content:
5:As these deployments scale, a critical failure mode has emerged that is qualitatively different from crashes or syntax errors: the agent \emph{stagnates}---continuing to produce actions that appear purposeful while making no meaningful progress toward the task goal.
7:Crucially, the dominant failure pattern is not simple repetition but what we term \emph{semantic stagnation}: the agent issues varied commands, edits different files, and generates plausible-looking outputs, yet its behavior is functionally stuck.
9:We observe this phenomenon at scale: across trajectories from two architecturally distinct agents---SWE-Agent \citep{yang2024sweagent} and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands}---on SWE-bench tasks \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, 28.5\% and 6.6\% of sliding windows exhibit stagnation under our silver labeling scheme, respectively, confirming that the failure mode is both prevalent and highly agent-dependent.
12:First, \emph{repetition detectors} such as cycle detection \citep{george2025cycledetection} and SpecRA \citep{pipis2025reasoningloop} identify structural repetition---exact or near-exact loops in action sequences---but by design miss semantically diverse stagnation where the agent varies its surface behavior while remaining functionally stuck.
13:Second, \emph{step-level scoring} via process reward models \citep{xi2025agentprm} evaluates individual actions in isolation, discarding the window-level temporal dynamics that distinguish transient setbacks from sustained stagnation---a distinction that requires reasoning over sequences of consecutive actions \citep{chen2025monitoring}.
16:More fundamentally, none of these approaches asks the prior question: \emph{what signals actually carry stagnation information?}
20:Using a weak supervision framework \citep{ratner2016dataprogramming,ratner2017snorkel}, we construct silver-labeled datasets from over 205K windows spanning SWE-Agent (54,809 windows, 28.5\% silver-labeled stagnation) and OpenHands (150,652 windows, 6.6\% stagnation).
23:Our window-level formulation ($k{=}5$ consecutive actions, stride 1) captures short-range temporal patterns---such as repeated failures followed by strategy changes---that step-level approaches cannot express, while providing the granularity to pinpoint \emph{when} stagnation begins and ends within a trajectory, enabling targeted interventions.
36:On SWE-Agent, command repetition ($\lambda_1$) leads stagnation onset by 1.87 steps, file diff ($\lambda_2$) is near-concurrent at $-1.20$ steps, and outcome backpropagation ($\lambda_3$) lags by 6.70 steps.
47:    \item \textbf{Structural signal discovery.} We demonstrate that 30 lightweight structural features achieve near-perfect stagnation detection (0.9951 in-domain, 0.967 cross-agent macro-F1), outperforming neural probes and LLM judges by wide margins (+33.3\,pp over LLM-as-judge), with no GPU and under 5\,ms per window. This redirects agent monitoring from costly representation learning toward lightweight structural approaches.
48:    \item \textbf{Labeling function temporal dynamics.} We reveal that labeling functions occupy statistically distinct temporal niches relative to stagnation onset, with agent-specific reversals that corrupt silver labels when transferred across architectures, informing future weak-supervision design on sequential agent data.
